summary: Children, spouse, parents, siblings and grandparents have a protected share of half or one third of their statutory share (Civil Code art. 1223). A foreign national's estate follows their national law. Taiwan has a Trust Act but is not in the Hague Trusts Convention, and foundations are public-interest only.
reserved_share: Descendants, parents and spouse: one half of their statutory share; siblings and grandparents: one third (Civil Code art. 1223).
foreign_law_note: Act Governing the Choice of Law in Civil Matters art. 58: succession is governed by the law of the deceased's nationality at death. A foreign national therefore keeps national law by default. I did not read the article text and a proviso for property in Taiwan may apply.
trust_note: Not on the HCCH status table (Taiwan is not a party). The Trust Act (1996) and the Trust Enterprise Act allow trusts; the Estate and Gift Tax Act and the Income Tax Act tax trusts by type. Foundations (Civil Code arts. 59-65) need approval from the authority and serve public-benefit goals; family foundations are not available.
open_questions: Read the text of the choice-of-law Act art. 58 and any proviso.
Confirm the Trust Act's tax articles (Estate and Gift Tax Act art. 3-2).
